findings.printedLatin: Rex Ardoinus sceptri moderamine fissus / Regnat in Hesperia, tendit in Ausoniam.
findings.englishAsRendered: King Arduin, upheld by the governance of the scepter, / Reigns in Hesperia, stretches toward Ausonia.
findings.conjecture: fissus > fisus ("relying on / confident in the governance of the scepter"); the doubled -ss- turns a participle of confidence into one of being split or broken.
findings.whyContradiction: The next line of the same distich asserts the opposite of a broken rule: "Regnat in Hesperia, tendit in Ausoniam" — Arduin is reigning and extending his reach, in the dating formula whose whole function is to fix the year 1003 by naming the king then securely on the throne. A king "split by the governance of the scepter" contradicts the very clause it introduces. Our English silently repairs it as "upheld by," which is fisus, not fissus — the printed defect is not visible to an English reader.
